iterations.title: Delay-gain driven multi-candidate gate sizing to eliminate critical-path slew degradation
iterations.hypothesis: Timing-critical paths across all benchmark designs suffer from severe transition slew degradation because SizeUpGenerator penalizes higher drive strengths by dividing delay gain by the cell area inflation ratio, forcing minimally sized replacements (X2) or leaving gates at X1. Furthermore, SizeUpGenerator generates only a single candidate per target, so any local placement legalization failure aborts sizing completely. By scoring candidate cells on timing-critical paths by pure stage delay reduction and returning a ranked multi-candidate set of viable drive strengths, the optimizer can evaluate and commit higher drive strengths (X4/X8) while gracefully falling back if OpenDP legalization fails. This directly sharpens transition slews on critical drivers and reduces both WNS and TNS.

evaluator.lesson: Candidate 0003 produced no timing evidence because the upsizeCell-to-upsizeCells API change broke test compilation, and all ten smoke logs failed during helper initialization.
evaluator.dead_end: Repeating the incompatible API rename without migrating callers will fail gates before timing evaluation.
bad_changes: SizeUpGenerator.hh replaced upsizeCell with upsizeCells while TestResizer.cc retained the old API, producing five compiler errors.
Smoke success reporting accepted ten logs containing missing helpers.tcl errors.

iterations.title: Isolate absolute delay-gain ranking with API-compatible single-candidate sizing
iterations.hypothesis: Cost-normalized sizing can prefer a smaller timing improvement over a larger eligible delay reduction on violating data paths. Preserve the champion upsizeCell API and single-candidate generation, but select the replacement with maximum positive finite stage delay gain, retaining the preceding-driver input-capacitance penalty and existing eligibility checks. AES critical X1 logic provides the clearest opportunity, while Ibex may benefit within its data cone; its fanout-943 clock gate is not evidence for this mechanism. Iteration 3 never reached timing evaluation, so this retry isolates ranking from candidate multiplicity and avoids its incompatible API rename. Improved selections should reduce matched-endpoint data arrivals and WNS/TNS, subject to upstream loading, hold, area, DRV, and placement gates.

evaluator.lesson: Absolute stage-gain ranking changed rising-edge replacement selection and failed unit gates before any benchmark timing benefit could be measured.
evaluator.dead_end: Repeating the same gate-failing absolute-gain selector without resolving its selection contract cannot produce evaluable timing evidence.
bad_changes: src/rsz/src/move/SizeUpGenerator.cc: replacing cost-normalized ranking with absolute gain conflicts with two existing rising-edge master assertions; timing impact is unmeasured.

iterations.title: Recover suppressed sizing moves with cost-ranked feasible replacement selection
iterations.hypothesis: The champion ranks replacement masters before checking instance-level upstream max-capacitance feasibility, so an infeasible winner can suppress a profitable feasible runner-up. Select the highest-scoring feasible master while preserving cost-normalized stage gain, upstream loading penalties, transition guards, the upsizeCell API, and single-candidate generation. Iteration 4 identifies this search limitation but provides no benchmark timing evidence; iteration 3 establishes the API-compatibility failure this implementation avoids. Recovered sizing should reduce matched data-path arrivals on affected AES or Ibex endpoints without increasing logic depth. If no feasible-runner-up opportunities occur in tier A, the mechanism is inapplicable and should be rejected.

evaluator.lesson: Moving upstream max-capacitance feasibility into sizing selection preserved compatibility but produced zero incremental tier-A timing benefit.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat feasible-runner-up sizing selection without measured recovery opportunities and attributable endpoint gains.
good_changes: src/move/SizeUpGenerator.cc and src/move/SizeUpGenerator.hh preserved the protected upsizeCell API; all supplied unit and smoke gates passed, but no timing benefit was measured.
bad_changes: src/move/SizeUpGenerator.cc moved replacementPreservesMaxCap into contender selection with zero measured WNS, TNS, or reported endpoint improvement.

iterations.title: Enable shared-critical-data rebuffering beyond the blanket fanout cutoff
iterations.hypothesis: BufferGenerator currently excludes every net with fanout at least 20, including confirmed Ibex data-path drivers with fanouts 22, 31, and 45. Preserve low-fanout behavior but admit higher-fanout setup data targets when at least two distinct immediate loads have finite negative setup slack for the target transition, retaining existing protections and excluding clock drivers. Reuse the existing required-time-aware rebuffer search to improve shared-load topology and reduce multiple endpoint arrivals. Iteration 5 supports this direction through measured sizing parity and unresolved shared data loads, while iteration 4 supplies the selection-contract failure to avoid without providing timing evidence. Success requires committed newly eligible repairs and attributable post-legalization WNS/TNS gains.

evaluator.lesson: High-fanout eligibility reduced Ibex TNS by 3.52% but failed promotion because AES regressed and retained repairs on the intended drivers were not established.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat fanout eligibility expansion without retained-driver attribution and post-legalization collateral checks.
good_changes: src/rsz/src/move/BufferGenerator.cc preserves low-fanout eligibility, net protections, and clock exclusion; GCD timing remained identical.
The eligibility-only candidate reduced Ibex TNS by 14.636 ns, but the specific retained rebuffer mechanism remains unverified.
bad_changes: src/rsz/src/move/BufferGenerator.cc enables high-fanout candidates by default without demonstrating post-legalization benefit across affected branches; AES WNS and TNS regressed.
Reusing BufferCandidate and Rebuffer unchanged did not establish retained repairs on fanout-22/31/45 targets or meet the 20 ps Ibex WNS target.

iterations.title: Choose split-load partitions by branch slack budgets instead of half the sink count
iterations.hypothesis: The champion isolates half the headroom-ranked sinks without evaluating their capacitance or inserted-buffer delay. Search nonempty proper prefixes while retaining the focus-path sink directly on the driver, predicting the existing target-slew buffer size and both-transition branch arrival changes. Reject partitions that worsen already-negative moved-load slack or create negative slack on previously nonnegative moved loads, then maximize predicted worst-load slack improvement with aggregate negative-slack improvement as a tie-breaker. Iteration 6 supports investigating shared-load repair but warns against eligibility expansion and unverified retention; iteration 5 establishes the sizing fallback dead end this plan avoids. Retained splits should reduce shared data-driver delay and improve multiple matched endpoints after legalization.

evaluator.lesson: Capacitance-aware prefix selection with predicted moved-load safety regressed AES WNS by 5.341 ps and TNS by 0.984591 ns, so split retention requires measured affected-endpoint checks after legalization.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat prediction-only prefix replacement without attributing retained splits and verifying post-legalization collateral.
bad_changes: src/rsz/src/move/SplitLoadGenerator.cc: prefix selection replacement regressed AES and produced no measured GCD or Ibex benefit
src/rsz/src/move/SplitLoadGenerator.cc: HPWL capacitance and gate-delay prediction omits wire resistance and downstream slew propagation

iterations.title: Select LEGACY path repairs by journaled measured WNS/TNS gain
iterations.hypothesis: The champion tries load-delay-ranked drivers and accepts the first applicable move before comparing its endpoint impact with alternatives. Replace this decision in LEGACY path repair with deterministic journaled trials of existing legal candidates from the same checkpoint. After parasitic and STA refresh, admit only candidates that preserve global WNS, global TNS, and focus-endpoint slack, then maximize delta WNS plus delta TNS divided by the constrained endpoint count. Iteration 6 supports investigating shared endpoint benefit through its 14.636 ns Ibex TNS improvement, while iteration 7 demonstrates the collateral risk of prediction-only selection. Reapply and verify the winner, and require its gains to survive final detailed placement.

iterations.title: Rank repair targets by slack-weighted count of violating endpoints sharing each driver (multi-endpoint path-sharing) instead of per-path load delay
iterations.hypothesis: Stock SetupLegacyBase::rankPathDrivers orders drivers on a single endpoint's worst path by local load-dependent delay, so a driver on hundreds of violating paths (Ibex _26153_/ZN, fanout 943) gets no priority over a driver on one path. Build a deterministic, capped (top 400 violators, refreshed every 25 endpoints) shared-criticality map summing normalised negative slack of every violating endpoint whose worst path passes through each driver, and rank targets by load_delay*(1+share). Acceptance, generators and repair budget stay stock, avoiding iteration 8's admission/trial machinery that collapsed AES's move mix and timed out JPEG. Each move on a high-share driver improves many endpoints at once, so TNS should drop sharply on Ibex/JPEG while AES (diffuse sharing) stays near stock. RSZ_EVOLVE counters will report builds, rank changes and build time.

evaluator.lesson: Shared-criticality ranking reduced Ibex TNS magnitude by 52.28% but changed repair trajectories enough to worsen AES and JPEG, so sharing needs bounded influence and evidence of structural concentration.
evaluator.dead_end: Applying load_delay*(1+share) broadly while keeping acceptance and generators stock does not preserve the move mix or protect QoR.

iterations.title: Criticality-weighted (Lagrangian-style) cell selection that charges upstream and side-load delay by their violation weight
iterations.hypothesis: Stock SizeUpGenerator picks a replacement master from a single-stage delay estimate on the repaired path, treating upstream and side-load collateral as unweighted, which explains AES/JPEG regressions in iterations 8-9 where shared local drivers (e.g. AES _13069_/Z) degraded. Replace the selection score with sum over affected arcs of lambda_arc * delta_delay, where lambda = max(0,-slack)/|WNS| for the target arc, the upstream driver arc (input-cap increase) and side loads of the input net. With no violating neighbours the score reduces to stock ranking, preserving unit-test contracts that broke iteration 4. Masters that steal slack from critical neighbours lose; sizes on targets with slack-rich upstream win, improving TNS in shared cones without the WNS damage of ranking-based approaches.

evaluator.lesson: Neighbour weighting activated on 5078 of 5086 size selections but changed only 23 choices, improving AES TNS by 0.007183 ns without WNS gain; prioritize shared-net topology repair.
evaluator.dead_end: Repeating capped input-capacitance penalty tuning within unchanged stock eligibility does not address the measured Ibex and JPEG bottlenecks.
good_changes: src/rsz/src/move/SizeUpGenerator.cc: counters distinguish weighted-score activation from actual master-choice changes.
src/rsz/src/move/SizeUpGenerator.cc: retaining stock eligibility and zero-neighbour scoring fallback preserved passing compatibility gates.
bad_changes: src/rsz/src/move/SizeUpGenerator.cc: capped aggregate neighbour weighting changed no JPEG choices and yielded no Ibex timing improvement.
src/rsz/src/move/SizeUpGenerator.cc: selecting a replacement despite a negative weighted score prevents explicit rejection of predicted collateral loss.

iterations.title: TNS-aware van Ginneken: carry per-option total sink violation and choose the lowest-TNS tree among those within epsilon of the best worst-sink slack
iterations.hypothesis: Rebuffer::rebufferNet scores buffer-tree options only by (load cap, earliest required time) and picks the root option with the largest worst-sink slack, so on shared nets with many violating sinks it ignores total violation. We add a third Pareto dimension V (sum of sink violation, propagated piecewise-linearly through wires/buffers via a violating-sink count and summed at junctions) and choose, among root options within epsilon=min(1ps, 5%|S*|) of the stock-best slack, the one with the lowest V. This captures the shared-endpoint TNS benefit seen in iterations 8/9 locally per net, without the global target reordering that broke AES/JPEG, and without the eligibility expansion (iter 6) or split-partition prediction (iter 7) dead ends. With at most one violating sink it reduces exactly to stock. Expected: Ibex/JPEG TNS improves on shared-net cones while WNS stays within 1 ps.

evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat global endpoint reordering or promote uninstrumented root-only V reranking as a substitute for three-dimensional Pareto retention.
bad_changes: src/rsz/src/Rebuffer.cc: chooseLowestTnsOption reranking coincided with AES TNS regression and no Ibex timing benefit; causality is unverified.

iterations.title: TNS-weighted lexicographic acceptance (WNS guard band + design TNS gain) replacing endpoint-only slack acceptance in the LEGACY repair loop
iterations.hypothesis: Stock LEGACY repair keeps a speculative move only if the targeted endpoint's slack improves, so shared-cone moves that help many violating endpoints (Ibex _26153_ trunk) are rolled back while locally-helpful moves that hurt side paths (AES regressions in iters 7/9/11) are kept. Replace this with a lexicographic rule using OpenSTA's incrementally maintained design WNS/TNS: reject if design or endpoint WNS worsens by more than 1 ps, otherwise accept when dTNS + lambda*dSlack_endpoint > 0 (lambda = violators/4), and veto stock-accepted moves whose TNS loss exceeds 2x their endpoint gain. Target ranking and move generators stay stock, which avoids the trajectory collapse of iteration 9 and the exhaustive-search timeout of iteration 8. The rule reduces exactly to stock when the TNS change equals the endpoint's own change. Expect Ibex TNS to improve by more than 10 ns, AES TNS to stop regressing, and JPEG to stay near stock.

evaluator.lesson: TNS-aware pass promotion improved Ibex TNS by 11.627 ns, but rolling checkpoint guards and stock-pass vetoes worsened WNS on every design and failed to protect AES.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat the combined rolling 1 ps guard, violator-weighted acceptance, and 2x TNS-loss veto as a global threshold-tuning experiment.
good_changes: Design-TNS-aware checkpoint promotion in src/rsz/src/policy/SetupLegacyPolicy.cc coincided with Ibex's 11.627 ns TNS gain; isolate its four acceptance flips before retaining it.
bad_changes: Rolling 1 ps WNS tolerance in src/rsz/src/policy/SetupLegacyPolicy.cc does not impose a cumulative WNS budget.
Stock-pass TNS-loss veto in src/rsz/src/policy/SetupLegacyPolicy.cc fired 585 times on AES without preventing worse final WNS and TNS.
Combined acceptance changes altered repair trajectories despite unchanged target ranking and move generators.

iterations.title: Two-phase repair: unchanged stock LEGACY loop, then a bottleneck-driven TNS-recovery phase with a hard post-stock WNS floor
iterations.hypothesis: Every in-loop change so far (iters 8, 9, 12) found large Ibex TNS gains from shared-cone/TNS-aware repair but perturbed the stock trajectory and lost WNS on AES/gcd/JPEG. Instead of modifying the greedy worst-path-first loop, run it unchanged, snapshot design WNS W*, then run a separate phase that ranks driver pins by the slack-weighted count of violating paths through them (top-N=400 paths) and trials stock generator moves on the top-K drivers under a journal, keeping a move only if design WNS >= W* (absolute, non-rolling) and measured design TNS improves by >= 0.5 ps. Rounds repeat with re-ranking until no move is kept, 5 rounds pass, or a move cap of max(30, 10% of stock moves) is hit. This makes final WNS >= stock by construction while harvesting shared-trunk TNS (e.g. the Ibex _26153_ fanout-943 trunk, the JPEG HA/FA drivers), and moves on shared drivers of the worst cone can also raise WNS.

evaluator.lesson: A separate journaled TNS recovery phase with a fixed stock-WNS floor improved WNS on all four designs and reduced Ibex TNS by 32.39%, while still permitting individual endpoint regressions.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not reintroduce shared-cone/TNS ranking inside the stock greedy loop: iterations 8, 9 and 12 traded Ibex gains for AES/gcd/JPEG WNS losses.
good_changes: src/rsz/src/policy/SetupLegacyPolicy.cc::runTnsRecovery preserves the stock trajectory and ranks shared drivers for a separate recovery phase
Fixed stock-WNS acceptance, measured incremental TNS acceptance and journal rollback filter harmful recovery trials
bad_changes: Global WNS/TNS acceptance permits local losses, including Ibex instr_addr_o[22] becoming violating
Top-50 coverage, three attempts per driver and fixed within-round ranking may limit search; this is not established as the cause of endpoint regressions

iterations.title: Joint path-window sizing by dynamic programming as a compound move inside the post-stock TNS-recovery phase
iterations.hypothesis: Remaining violations sit on deep HA/FA (JPEG) and fanout-943-trunk (Ibex) paths where one-cell-at-a-time upsizing is cancelled by the extra input-cap load on the upstream stage, so recovery rejects most single moves (77 WNS rejects on JPEG). Replace greedy single-driver master selection with a Viterbi-style dynamic program over a 4-stage window of the worst path. It chooses masters jointly using load-aware arc delays plus a violation-weighted side-load penalty, and applies the result as one journaled compound move. The move is offered only inside runTnsRecovery, under the unchanged fixed stock-WNS floor and 0.5 ps TNS threshold, so the stock trajectory is preserved. Coordinated sizing should turn rejected single moves into accepted joint moves and raise the recovery keep rate on JPEG and Ibex.

evaluator.lesson: Joint sizing under a fixed stock-WNS floor displaced recovery moves and improved Ibex TNS by 21.20% versus champion while surrendering 5.205 ps of Ibex WNS and 1.289 ps of JPEG WNS.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat default-slew four-stage master-only DP before fallback recovery under only a fixed stock-WNS floor; JPEG rejected 49 of 75 DP trials for WNS and retained the same 34 total recovery moves.
good_changes: src/rsz/src/policy/SetupLegacyPolicy.cc compound journals and measured STA acceptance retained 15 Ibex and 14 JPEG DP trials, though their isolated TNS contribution is unmeasured

iterations.title: TNS-weighted critical-sink isolation with measured cut-point search on shared bottleneck nets, inside the post-stock recovery phase
iterations.hypothesis: Shared high-fanout nets (Ibex _26153_/ZN fanout 943, JPEG ddin[8]/Q) dominate the remaining violations, and the stock SplitLoad/Clone recipes split them by half-count local slack inside the greedy loop with predicted effect only. Instead, after the unchanged stock loop, rank shared bottleneck drivers by violating-endpoint count times summed negative slack, weight each sink by the downstream negative endpoint slack it carries, and try up to four cut points (keep the top-k critical sinks on the driver, move the rest behind a centroid-placed buffer or a clone, then optionally resize the driver), each evaluated by journaled incremental STA. Commit the best variant only if WNS >= max(stock-final WNS, last committed recovery WNS) and design TNS strictly improves. This runs on its own budget before the champion's existing recovery moves, so it does not displace them. Removing non-critical load from shared trunks should cut stage delay for every violating endpoint behind the net at once, delivering the shared-cone TNS gains of iterations 8 and 9 without perturbing the stock trajectory.

evaluator.lesson: Immediate-sink model-ranked SplitLoad cuts inside the stock loop regressed champion-relative score; test downstream-weighted cuts in an isolated measured phase with a monotonic WNS floor.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat greedy-loop cut reranking with a first-order RC model and one lowest-drive buffer at the driver location.

iterations.title: Lagrangian endpoint pricing with best-of-k measured moves and a ratcheting WNS floor in the post-stock TNS-recovery phase
iterations.hypothesis: The champion's post-stock recovery (runTnsRecovery) ranks drivers with a memoryless shared-driver score and accepts the first improving move against a fixed stock-WNS floor, so it saturates on Ibex's fanout-943 driver, rarely reaches JPEG's independent deep arithmetic cones, and gives back WNS (iterations 14, 15). Replace it with a multiplicative-weights Lagrangian loop: each violating endpoint carries a price lambda_e that grows while it stays violated, drivers are ranked by the lambda-weighted sum over their deduplicated downstream endpoints, and each chosen driver gets best-of-k measured evaluation across the existing size/swap/clone/split generators from one journal checkpoint. Commits must satisfy a ratcheting WNS floor max(stock-final, best-so-far) and a per-endpoint veto protecting high-price endpoints. The stock loop stays byte-identical; a 600-trial or 6-round budget bounds runtime, avoiding iteration 8's timeout.

evaluator.lesson: Multiplicative endpoint prices retained Ibex's shared-driver bias and worsened TNS magnitude by 28.53% versus champion; isolate cone diversity and structural move coverage before retuning prices.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat the bundled lambda-sum recovery replacement with only higher price growth or larger search budgets.

iterations.title: Required-time-ordered (LT-tree) fanout tree synthesis for shared high-fanout drivers as a measured move in the post-stock recovery phase
iterations.hypothesis: Ibex's worst paths all cross AND2_X1 _26153_/ZN with fanout 943, which stock repair never buffers and the champion's recovery phase only sizes or clones. Replace this with Touati-style timing-driven fanout trees: sort sinks by STA required time, keep the most critical group directly on a resized driver within a load-cap budget, and push less critical groups behind buffers placed at group centroids and chosen from all buffer masters. Several trees per net are built and judged on measured incremental STA inside a journal, under a ratcheting WNS floor plus a local guard for endpoints that start near zero slack. Only the champion's post-stock recovery phase runs this, so the stock trajectory stays byte-identical. Removing hundreds of pins of load from critical sinks should cut stage delay and slew on the shared trunk and improve TNS across thousands of Ibex endpoints without giving back WNS elsewhere.

evaluator.lesson: Zero applied trees and unchanged fanout 943 mean candidate 0017 did not test timing-driven load isolation; establish activation and measure feasible journaled variants before tuning the heuristic.
evaluator.dead_end: The current maximum-four-group lumped-RC prefilter produced zero applied trees and zero gain versus champion.

iterations.title: Measured best-of-k criticality-partitioned gate cloning (critical-sink replica + stock van Ginneken on tolerant sinks) for shared high-fanout drivers in the post-stock recovery phase
iterations.hypothesis: Shared high-fanout drivers on violating paths (Ibex AND2_X1 _26153_ with 943 loads on all ten worst paths; JPEG fanout 12-17 launch drivers) make every critical path pay the full net load, and the stock spatial 2-way clone or single-buffer split never restructures them; iteration 17's lumped-RC tree prefilter applied zero trees. Instead, in runTnsRecovery only, explicitly schedule drivers with fanout >=12, sort sinks by required time, and generate up to 6 atomic variants: a critical-only upsized replica (top 5/15/30% of sinks) or an m-way required-time-quantile clone split (m=2..4), with the tolerant net rebuffered by the stock Rebuffer::rebufferNet. Every variant is evaluated by journaled incremental STA and the best design-TNS variant is kept only if it satisfies a ratcheting WNS floor, a per-endpoint guard (pre-move slack > -1 ps must stay > -1 ps) and no new DRV. Cloning removes load from critical sinks without adding a buffer stage, so deep (33-37 stage) Ibex paths gain tens of ps at the shared stage across thousands of endpoints while measured selection avoids the model/STA mismatch of iterations 15 and 17.

evaluator.lesson: Iteration 18 lost to champion because visit-dependent single-replica cloning did not implement the proposed atomic search, while Ibex's 943-load attributed driver belongs to the launch clock path rather than the data chain.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not repeat same-strength critical-fraction clone rotation without isolated atomic evaluation and verified data-path targeting.

iterations.title: Measured depth-2 beam search over coupled sizing sequences on data-path-only bottleneck stages, with ratcheting WNS floor and per-endpoint guard, in the post-stock recovery phase
iterations.hypothesis: The remaining WNS/TNS lies on deep FA/HA/AOI data chains (Ibex [703]: six FA_X1 arcs ~679 ps; JPEG 20-23 stage multiplier paths), where single-stage upsizes are rejected because their input-cap penalty needs a matching upstream resize. Replace runTnsRecovery's first-improving single-move greedy with a measured beam search: seed stages are ranked by slack-weighted violating-endpoint coverage times arc delay over launch-Q-to-D data arcs only (clock-network pins such as Ibex _26153_ excluded). For each seed, single moves and depth-2 sequences (stage + upstream driver or downstream stage) are evaluated by journaled incremental STA from one restored checkpoint, and only the best sequence per round is committed. Acceptance uses a ratcheting WNS floor and rejects any sequence that pushes an endpoint above -1 ps below -1 ps. This should capture the coupled TNS gains iter 14's DP found while avoiding its WNS losses and iter 13/18's endpoint collateral.

evaluator.lesson: Measured depth-2 recovery improved JPEG baseline TNS by 0.525 ns but lost champion recovery because AES generated no trials and Ibex failed replay.
evaluator.dead_end: Do not replace champion greedy recovery with a fixed top-eight beam that regenerates moves during replay and cannot resize its dominant FA_X1/HA_X1 seeds.
